report.summary: All three UI tests fail the same way: Page.goto('/books') hits the 5 s timeout in tests/ui/conftest.py. The app's list_books() sleeps for a random 0-8 s (app/main.py:150) and render_books() calls it on every /books render (app/main.py:256), so the page sometimes takes longer than the timeout. This is flakiness, not a product or test bug; the first fix is to remove or bound that artificial delay so the page renders well under 5 s.

causes.title: /books render includes a random 0-8 s sleep, which exceeds the 5 s navigation timeout about 3 times in 8
causes.explanation: list_books() calls time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8)) before querying the database (app/main.py:149-150). render_books() calls list_books() for the /books page (app/main.py:256), so every page load waits a random 0-8 s. The UI fixture sets page.set_default_timeout(5000) (tests/ui/conftest.py:7), and tests/support/pages.py:34 calls page.goto('/books') with the default 'load' wait. Whenever the sleep draw is above about 5 s, which happens roughly 3/8 of the time, goto times out. The outcome depends on random chance, so the same commit can pass on a rerun. The three tests share this one root cause. The sleep only affects the HTML page; the API tests use the same list_books() but are not failing here. I found no other delay on this path, and the Page.goto call logs show a plain navigation with no server error. This is the only mechanism in the code that produces a 5 s timeout here. The test_login_ui tests that also visit /books are not in this failure list, which fits a random pass.
evidence: app/main.py:149-150: def list_books(user_id: int) -> list[dict]: / time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8))
app/main.py:250-261: render_books(...) builds "books": list_books(user["id"]) on every render
app/main.py:310-314: @app.get("/books") def books_page(...) returns render_books(request, user)
tests/ui/conftest.py:6-7: "Nothing in this app should take longer than 5 s" / page.set_default_timeout(5000)

Failure output for all three tests: "playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded." / "navigating to \"http://127.0.0.1:49185/books\", waiting until \"load\"" (ports 49184 and 49185)
The failure logs show only the navigation timeout. They contain no HTTP status or app traceback, so the server-side sleep is inferred from the code rather than seen in the logs.
causes.suggested_fix: First, delete the time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8)) line in app/main.py:150, since it looks like a deliberate slowness injection that should not be in the app. If the slowness is meant to test resilience, move it behind an explicit opt-in setting used only by a dedicated test. Second, make the UI tests wait for the app's real readiness rather than relying on 'load' under a 5 s budget. For example, have tests/support/pages.py wait for a book-list element after goto, and give the open() call a longer timeout only where the slowness is intended. Finally, rerun the UI suite several times to confirm the failures stop.
